```{r setup, include=FALSE}
render_started <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
library(bdynets)
source("prepare.R", local = TRUE)

plain_output <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  plain_output(gsub("[ \t]+\n", "\n", x, perl = TRUE), options)
})

figure_dir <- tempfile("metropolis-demo-figures-")
dir.create(figure_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE,
  fig.path = file.path(figure_dir, "figure-"), fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 7.5, dpi = 150, out.width = "100%"
)

raw_directory <- "data/raw"
prepared_file <- "data/input.rds"
selection_file <- "data/raw/selected-roads.csv"
calibration_file <- "data/raw/calibration.csv"
source_day <- "2024-10-18"
source_minutes <- seq(0, 25, 5)
source_files <- list.files("data", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)
source_files <- source_files[!grepl("/basemap-cache/", source_files)]
source_before <- tools::md5sum(source_files)
day_standard <- readRDS(prepared_file)
```

This tutorial follows the same complete workflow as the Beijing tutorial:

**understand the source → inspect and validate raw records → construct `standard` with `traffic_input()` → visualize `standard` with `traffic_map()` → validate → export and read back.**

City-traffic-M-specific code reads Parquet fields, validates the exact five-minute grid, applies recorded aggregation and fill rules, and creates canonical tables. The public constructor and plotting functions remain general.

## Data, source, and preparation goal

City Traffic Benchmarks version 4 supplies five-minute road volume and speed for Yekaterinburg. This case retains the existing 720-road register and the complete source day of 18 October 2024. The selected-day method produces 96 fifteen-minute frames.

Volume retains the declared unit `source volume`; the Parquet files do not supply a physical volume unit or timezone. Speed values are retained as supplied. A derived congestion index combines slowdown relative to full-history nonzero speed P90 with clipped log-volume weight relative to the selected-day frame-volume P95.

```{r source-summary, echo=FALSE}
original_sources <- read.csv("data/original-sources.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  original_sources[c("file", "provider", "role")],
  caption = "Original data sources",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Item = c("Roads", "Fifteen-minute frames", "Flow records", "Additional measurement records", "Trend records", "Primary unit"),
    Value = c(
      nrow(day_standard[["roads"]]), length(day_standard[["times"]]),
      nrow(day_standard[["flow"]]), nrow(day_standard[["measurements"]]),
      nrow(day_standard[["trends"]]), day_standard[["unit"]]
    )
  ),
  caption = "Complete prepared dataset",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
```

The road register and date are fixed source selections for this example; the conversion does not choose new roads or a different day.

The preparation goal is to retain the supplied 720-road selection, preserve native missing/observed/imputed status, aggregate three five-minute slots into each fifteen-minute frame, retain volume and speed without inventing physical units, compute the documented congestion index, and produce descriptive maps and trends.

This is the current 720-road City-traffic-M lineage. The older 142-segment simulated fallback is a separate historical demonstration and is not used here.

## Raw input, field meanings, and editable configuration

### Configuration to edit

```{r configuration}
raw_directory <- "data/raw"
prepared_file <- "data/input.rds"
selection_file <- "data/raw/selected-roads.csv"
calibration_file <- "data/raw/calibration.csv"
source_day <- "2024-10-18"
source_minutes <- seq(0, 25, 5)
frame_minutes <- 15L
primary_unit <- "source volume"  # Physical volume units are not verified.
selected_time <- params$time_label
```

Changing the selected road file or date changes the scientific scope and requires new validation. Do not replace `primary_unit` with vehicles or vehicles/hour unless the provider documentation establishes that unit.

### Inspect the original-format teaching excerpt

The teaching excerpt reads two original Parquet road IDs—21263 and 2565—and six five-minute slots from 00:00 through 00:25. The full-history calibration remains attached to those roads.

```{r read-raw}
native <- read_metropolis_raw(
  base = ".",
  raw_dir = raw_directory,
  selection_file = selection_file,
  day = source_day,
  minutes = source_minutes,
  calibration_file = calibration_file
)
```

```{r show-raw, echo=FALSE}
static_rows <- data.frame(static_row0 = native[["ids"]], native[["static"]])
volume_rows <- data.frame(
  timestamp = native[["labels"]],
  t(native[["volume"]]), check.names = FALSE
)
speed_rows <- data.frame(
  timestamp = native[["labels"]],
  t(native[["speed"]]), check.names = FALSE
)
names(volume_rows)[-1] <- names(speed_rows)[-1] <- paste0("node_", native[["ids"]])

knitr::kable(static_rows, caption = "Original static Parquet rows", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(volume_rows, caption = "Original five-minute volume", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(speed_rows, caption = "Original five-minute speed", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)

calibration <- read.csv(calibration_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  calibration,
  caption = "Retained speed and volume calibration",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)

field_dictionary <- data.frame(
  Source_field = c("static row position", "x/y start and end", "length", "timestamp", "node_ID volume", "node_ID speed", "history speed P90", "frame volume P95"),
  Meaning = c("Zero-based road identifier", "Directed endpoint coordinates", "Source road length", "Five-minute source clock", "Native source volume", "Native source speed", "Free-flow reference", "Volume-weight reference"),
  Standard_destination = c("road_id", "roads geometry", "retained road attribute", "fifteen-minute time", "flow", "measurements: speed", "provenance and index", "provenance and index")
)
knitr::kable(field_dictionary, caption = "Key source fields", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

Missing speed remains distinct from observed zero volume. The source adapter retains native coverage masks, contributor counts, and fill methods in provenance.

#### Native source object and readback {.unnumbered}

The intermediate `source.rds` retains native IDs, clocks and observations. This sample snapshot is saved and read back in a temporary directory; the supplied day-level snapshot stays unchanged.

```{r native-source, echo=FALSE}
native_directory <- tempfile("native-source-")
dir.create(native_directory)
native_file <- file.path(native_directory, "source.rds")
stopifnot(!file.exists(native_file))
```

```{r native-source-2, echo=TRUE}
saveRDS(native, native_file, compress = "xz", version = 3)
restored_native <- readRDS(native_file)
```

```{r native-source-3, echo=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(restored_native, native))
native <- restored_native
invisible(capture.output(str(native, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = basename(native_file), schema = native$schema, exact_readback = TRUE),
    caption = "Native source snapshot before standard-input construction", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

The intermediate object retains source detail; the next step constructs the common road, value and time tables.

### Deliberately invalid timestamps and correction

The fifteen-minute conversion requires unique, ordered five-minute timestamps. The following in-memory copy duplicates the first timestamp and therefore breaks the exact grid; the Parquet files are unchanged.

```{r invalid-input}
bad_labels <- native$labels
bad_labels[2] <- bad_labels[1]
cat(tryCatch(
  {
    metropolis_bins(native$volume, bad_labels)
    "No error was raised."
  },
  error = conditionMessage
))
```

The corrected labels are the six unique, consecutive timestamps read from the source. Missing cells are retained in the native status mask; they are not automatically interpreted as observed zero.

```{r corrected-input-check}
corrected_bins <- metropolis_bins(native$volume, native$labels)
stopifnot(length(unique(native$labels)) == length(native$labels))
data.frame(
  roads = nrow(native$volume),
  five_minute_slots = ncol(native$volume),
  fifteen_minute_frames = length(corrected_bins$times),
  native_missing = sum(is.na(native$volume)),
  observed_zero = sum(native$volume == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

## Convert with the general bdynets interface

`metropolis_input()` is an **example adapter**, not a public package API. It implements this source's fifteen-minute averaging, recorded fill rules, geometry construction, speed measurement, congestion-index calculation, and source trends. The resulting canonical tables are then passed to the public constructor.

### Prepare canonical tables

```{r prepare-canonical-tables}
adapter_output <- metropolis_input(native)

roads <- adapter_output[["roads"]]
flow <- adapter_output[["flow"]]
measurements <- adapter_output[["measurements"]]
trends <- adapter_output[["trends"]]
times <- adapter_output[["times"]]
time_labels <- adapter_output[["time_labels"]]
interval_seconds <- adapter_output[["interval_seconds"]]
```

Once the canonical tables exist, the public call is the same interface used by other road datasets:

### Construct `standard` with `traffic_input()`

```{r construct-standard-input}
standard <- bdynets::traffic_input(
  roads = roads,
  flow = flow,
  measurements = measurements,
  metric_info = adapter_output[["metric_info"]],
  trends = trends,
  times = times,
  time_labels = time_labels,
  interval_seconds = interval_seconds,
  unit = adapter_output[["unit"]],
  provenance = adapter_output[["provenance"]],
  title = adapter_output[["title"]],
  description = "Fifteen-minute City-traffic-M source volume, speed, and derived congestion index.",
  preparation = c(
    "Validate the unique consecutive five-minute source grid.",
    "Average three source slots into each fifteen-minute frame.",
    "Retain native coverage, contributor counts, and recorded fill methods.",
    "Compute the documented congestion index without assigning a source label."
  )
)
```

The returned object is a named list with schema `bdynets-traffic-input-v1`. It contains the primary `flow` table, additional speed and congestion measurements, supplied trends, timing, units, and provenance.

### What does `standard` contain?

```{r standard-structure}
str(standard, max.level = 1, give.attr = FALSE)
```

```{r show-standard, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  standard[["roads"]][c("road_id", "length", "speedLimit", "freeFlowSpeed", "maxVolume")],
  caption = "Standard roads table",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  standard[["flow"]], caption = "Standard fifteen-minute flow table",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  standard[["measurements"]], caption = "Standard speed and congestion measurements",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  standard[["trends"]], caption = "Standard supplied trends",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
```

For road 21263, volumes 3, 6, and 5 produce first-quarter flow 4.67; the corresponding mean speed is 81.88 and the derived congestion index is 0.040. The index is computed as:

```text
slowdown = clip(1 - frame_speed / history_speed_P90, 0, 1)
weight   = clip(log1p(frame_volume) / log1p(frame_volume_P95), 0, 1)
index    = slowdown * weight
```

The index is derived from supplied data and calibration; it is not a congestion label present in the raw Parquets.

The conversion changes four things while retaining the source meaning:

- **Identifier and geometry:** zero-based static Parquet row IDs become character `road_id` values with directed start/end coordinates.
- **Time:** three complete five-minute slots become one fifteen-minute frame start.
- **Measurements:** volume remains `source volume`; speed remains `source speed`; congestion is explicitly marked as a derived dimensionless index.
- **Coverage metadata:** native observed, missing, and imputed status; contributor counts; fill methods; calibration; selection; and source identities remain in provenance.

<div class="note"><code>bdynets::traffic_input()</code> is the public constructor. The Metropolis adapter is source-specific, but its <code>roads</code>, <code>flow</code>, <code>measurements</code>, <code>trends</code>, and time arguments use the same standard package interface.</div>

### Adapt a teaching CSV with renamed columns

The small lesson CSV can be renamed by another data owner. An explicit mapping restores source roles before the same validation and conversion are applied.

```{r renamed-csv}
lesson_volume <- read.csv("data/lesson/volume.csv", check.names = FALSE)
incoming <- lesson_volume
names(incoming) <- c("source_time", paste0("volume_road_", native$ids))
column_mapping <- setNames(names(incoming), names(lesson_volume))

mapped_volume <- incoming[unname(column_mapping)]
names(mapped_volume) <- names(column_mapping)
stopifnot(identical(mapped_volume, lesson_volume))
head(incoming)
```

The mapping changes headers only. It does not change road IDs, timestamps, missingness, units, aggregation, or the public `traffic_input()` call.

## Pass the standard object to `traffic_map()`

The teaching object above contains two roads and two quarter-hour frames. The supplied full-day object was produced through the same interface and is used for the city map. It is passed directly to `traffic_map()`; `read_traffic()` is only used to create the analytical view required by `traffic_trend()`.

```{r plot-prepare}
index <- match(
  params[["time_label"]],
  sub("^.* ", "", day_standard[["time_labels"]])
)
if (is.na(index)) stop("The selected frame is not present.")

day_traffic <- read_traffic(prepared_file)

# Request the background explicitly: the global auto option is switched off
# below, so an "auto" argument would silently render without a basemap.
basemap_daily <- NULL
if (params[["basemap"]]) {
  basemap_daily <- traffic_basemap(day_traffic, road_classes = character())
}
options(bdynets.basemap.auto = FALSE)
```

### Road volume map

```{r road-map, fig.alt="Prepared City-traffic-M volume in the selected fifteen-minute frame."}
traffic_map(
  day_standard,
  index = index,
  basemap = basemap_daily,
  title = "City-traffic-M traffic volume",
  caption = "Prepared fifteen-minute road volume; missing values are grey."
)
```

### Daily mean road volume

```{r road-trend, fig.height=4.4}
flow_trend <- traffic_trend(day_traffic)
plot(flow_trend, metric = "mean", index = index)
```

The map and curve use the primary volume field. Observed zeros contribute to the mean and missing values are excluded. The curve is a mean across available roads, not a citywide vehicle total.

## Validate the conversion

```{r validation, echo=FALSE}
flow_at <- match(
  paste(standard[["flow"]][["road_id"]], standard[["flow"]][["time"]]),
  paste(day_standard[["flow"]][["road_id"]], day_standard[["flow"]][["time"]])
)
measurement_at <- match(
  paste(standard[["measurements"]][["road_id"]], standard[["measurements"]][["time"]], standard[["measurements"]][["metric"]]),
  paste(day_standard[["measurements"]][["road_id"]], day_standard[["measurements"]][["time"]], day_standard[["measurements"]][["metric"]])
)

validation <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "Teaching flow records agree with the complete standard day",
    "Teaching measurements agree with the complete standard day",
    "Complete flow row count equals roads multiplied by frames",
    "No duplicated road_id-time keys are present",
    "The current lineage contains exactly 720 selected roads",
    "The full day contains 96 unique consecutive fifteen-minute frames",
    "Unknown physical volume units remain explicit",
    "Native coverage and fill metadata are retained",
    "Observed primary values are finite and nonnegative",
    "Source files remain unchanged during report generation"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    !anyNA(flow_at) && identical(standard[["flow"]][["flow"]], day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]][flow_at]),
    !anyNA(measurement_at) && identical(standard[["measurements"]][["value"]], day_standard[["measurements"]][["value"]][measurement_at]),
    nrow(day_standard[["flow"]]) == nrow(day_standard[["roads"]]) * length(day_standard[["times"]]),
    !anyDuplicated(day_standard[["flow"]][c("road_id", "time")]),
    nrow(day_standard$roads) == 720,
    length(day_standard$times) == 96 && !anyDuplicated(day_standard$times) && all(diff(day_standard$times) == 900),
    identical(day_standard$unit, "source volume"),
    all(c("volume", "speed") %in% names(day_standard$provenance$native_coverage)),
    all(is.finite(day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]][!is.na(day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]])]) & day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]][!is.na(day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]])] >= 0),
    identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files))
  )
)
knitr::kable(validation, caption = "Core validation results", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)

coverage <- data.frame(
  Roads = nrow(day_standard[["roads"]]),
  Frames = length(day_standard[["times"]]),
  `Interval (minutes)` = unique(day_standard[["interval_seconds"]]) / 60,
  `Flow records` = nrow(day_standard[["flow"]]),
  `Measurement records` = nrow(day_standard[["measurements"]]),
  `Trend records` = nrow(day_standard[["trends"]]),
  `Missing flow` = sum(is.na(day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]])),
  `Observed zeros` = sum(day_standard[["flow"]][["flow"]] == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  Unit = day_standard[["unit"]],
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(coverage, caption = "Complete-data coverage", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)

native_coverage <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("volume", "speed"), function(key) {
  item <- day_standard$provenance$native_coverage[[key]]
  status <- as.integer(item$native_status)
  data.frame(
    Source = key,
    `Native missing cells` = sum(status == 0L),
    `Native observed nonzero cells` = sum(status == 1L),
    `Native observed zero cells` = sum(status == 2L),
    `Imputed fifteen-minute frames` = sum(item$frame_imputed),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(native_coverage, caption = "Native coverage retained separately from prepared availability", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

<div class="result">Every validation row must be <code>TRUE</code>. Prepared availability does not erase native missingness: native status, contributor counts, imputation flags, and fill methods remain in provenance and are reported separately.</div>

## Export, read back, and reuse

The teaching `standard` object is published to a new temporary directory. The export contains RDS and CSV tables, road vertices, a data dictionary, validation records, source identities, metadata, and checksums.

```{r prepared-export}
prepared_export_dir <- tempfile("metropolis-prepared-export-")
dictionary <- read.csv("data/data-dictionary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dictionary_key <- paste(dictionary$table, dictionary$field, sep = "/")
standard_key <- unlist(lapply(
  c("roads", "flow", "measurements", "trends"),
  function(table) paste(table, names(standard[[table]]), sep = "/")
))
dictionary <- dictionary[dictionary_key %in% standard_key, ]

declared_sources <- c(
  selection_file,
  calibration_file,
  file.path(raw_directory, paste0(
    "city-traffic-M-raw-",
    c("static-features", "volume", "speed"),
    ".parquet"
  ))
)
prepared_path <- write_traffic_input(
  standard,
  prepared_export_dir,
  source_files = declared_sources,
  native = native,
  dictionary = dictionary
)
restored <- readRDS(prepared_path)
```

```{r prepared-export-checks, echo=FALSE}
metadata <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "metadata.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE)
exported_flow <- read.csv(
  file.path(prepared_export_dir, "flow.csv"),
  na.strings = metadata$csv$missing,
  colClasses = c(road_id = "character")
)
manifest <- read.csv(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "checksums.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
core_fields <- setdiff(names(standard), "provenance")
export_checks <- data.frame(
  Check = c(
    "RDS core fields read back unchanged",
    "CSV IDs, times, values, and missingness read back correctly",
    "Dictionary and validation files are present",
    "Prepared-export checksums agree",
    "Source files remain unchanged"
  ),
  Passed = c(
    all(vapply(core_fields, function(key) identical(restored[[key]], standard[[key]]), logical(1))),
    identical(exported_flow$road_id, standard$flow$road_id) &&
      identical(as.numeric(exported_flow$time), as.numeric(standard$flow$time)) &&
      identical(is.na(exported_flow$flow), is.na(standard$flow$flow)) &&
      isTRUE(all.equal(exported_flow$flow, standard$flow$flow, check.attributes = FALSE)),
    all(file.exists(file.path(prepared_export_dir, c("data-dictionary.csv", "validation.csv")))),
    identical(
      unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(prepared_export_dir, manifest$file))),
      manifest$md5
    ),
    identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files))
  )
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = sort(list.files(prepared_export_dir))), caption = "Prepared-data export files", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(export_checks, caption = "Prepared-data readback checks", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(prepared_export_dir, "validation.csv")), caption = "Stored validation record", format = "html", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r optional-persistent-export}
if (params$export) {
  if (file.exists(params$export_dir)) stop("The requested export directory already exists; choose a new directory.")
  dir.create(params$export_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  write_traffic_input(
    standard,
    file.path(params$export_dir, "prepared-data"),
    source_files = declared_sources,
    native = native,
    dictionary = dictionary
  )
  traffic_export(
    day_traffic,
    file.path(params$export_dir, "figures"),
    index = index,
    input_files = c(prepared = prepared_file)
  )
}
```

## Reproduction, source records, and troubleshooting

Place this Rmd in `examples/metropolis/`. From the repository root, render it offline with:

```bash
Rscript -e "source('bdynets/inst/preparation-session.R'); preparation_session('examples/metropolis'); rmarkdown::render('examples/metropolis/metropolis-traffic-report-demo.Rmd', knit_root_dir='examples/metropolis', params=list(time_label='08:00', basemap=FALSE, export=FALSE))"
```

`basemap=FALSE` requires no network. Reading the original Parquets requires Python 3 with NumPy, pandas, and PyArrow; the supplied prepared object can be plotted in R without rerunning Python. With `basemap=TRUE`, verified caches may be reused, while a new background request requires network access.

Common problems include missing Python dependencies, duplicate or gapped timestamps, a road ID absent from the selected register, unknown speed-limit codes, invalid calibration, and reuse of an existing export directory. Physical volume units remain unresolved and must stay labelled `source volume`.

```{r reproducibility, echo=FALSE}
stopifnot(identical(source_before, tools::md5sum(source_files)))
knitr::kable(
  read.csv("data/original-sources.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[c("file", "provider", "role")],
  caption = "Original archives and source identities",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  read.csv("data/raw/source-manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[c("file", "selection")],
  caption = "Bundled Parquet projections and selections",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
conversion_files <- intersect(c("prepare.R", "read_parquet.py", "run.R"), list.files("."))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    file = conversion_files,
    sha256 = vapply(conversion_files, digest::digest, "", file = TRUE, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)
  ),
  caption = "Conversion and entry-point source identities",
  format = "html", row.names = FALSE
)
bundle_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "bdynets")
bundle_files <- list.files(bundle_dir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = FALSE)
bundle_sha <- vapply(file.path(bundle_dir, bundle_files), digest::digest, "", file = TRUE, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)
revision <- digest::digest(paste(paste(bundle_files, bundle_sha, sep = " "), collapse = "\n"), algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE)

cat("Package version:", as.character(packageVersion("bdynets")), "\n")
cat("Bundled source revision (SHA-256):", revision, "\n")
python_versions <- system2(
  "python3",
  c("-c", shQuote("import platform, numpy, pandas, pyarrow; print('Python', platform.python_version(), 'NumPy', numpy.__version__, 'pandas', pandas.__version__, 'PyArrow', pyarrow.__version__)")),
  stdout = TRUE, stderr = FALSE
)
cat(python_versions, sep = "\n")
cat("Report computation elapsed:", round(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - render_started, 1), "seconds\n")
sessionInfo()
```
